title: Live Cell Analysis of Shear Stress on Pseudomonas aeruginosa Using an Automated Higher-Throughput Microfluidic System
protocol: Mix 200 mL of sterile M9 salt solution with water.
Add 2 mL of sterile 1 M MgSO4 to the mixture.
Pipette 100 µL of sterile 1 M CaCl2 into the mixture.
Add 12.5 mL of sterile 20% (w/v) glucose to the solution.
Transfer the final volume to reach 1 L with water.
Sterilize a bottle and transfer the prepared minimal media into it using sterile techniques.
Place the bottle containing the media in an incubator or water bath set at the experimental temperature.
Ensure the media reaches the experiment temperature before use to prevent bubble formation in microchannels.
Inoculate 15 mL of experimental media in a sterile sidearm flask with one or two colonies from an agar plate streaked with PA01-EGFP.
Incubate the inoculated culture for 12-16 hours at 37 °C and 180-220 rpm on an incubator/shaker table.
Measure the OD600 of the overnight culture.
Dilute the overnight culture to a final OD of 0.8 using fresh MM when the OD600 is greater than 0.80.
Place the diluted experimental culture in an incubator or water bath at 37 °C until needed for seeding microfluidic channels.
Check the OD600 again immediately before seeding to ensure it remains close to the target value of 0.8.
Set up the system station according to the user guide.
Turn on the PC Workstation.
Activate the Fluorescence Module.
Ensure the fluorescence shutter is ON.
Start the Hardware Controllers.
Initiate the Imaging System Controller.
Power on the CCD Camera.
Operate the Imaging Station (Microscope).
Adjust the temperature of the heated plate to the desired experimental temperature.
Enter the plate number located on the label on the side of the plate in the control application.
Open the "Multi Dimensional Acquisition" menu on the microscope/imaging software window.
Set up the Control Module for an autorun.
Remove the 48-well microfluidic plate from packaging carefully.
Clean the glass slide at the bottom of the plate well with a lens tissue, lint free cloth, or low-lint wipe.
Pipette 200 µL of 37 °C MM into the output well.
Wipe the interface with ethanol and allow it to dry.
Seal the plate onto the plate stage in Manual Mode on the Control Module.
Set Fluid as LB at 37 °C and Max Shear at 5.00 dyne/cm2.
Click the output wells to activate flow from the output to the input well, priming the channels.
Pause the flow after 5 min of priming to prepare for seeding.
Remove the plate from the stage and pipette residual media from the output.
Pipette 300 µL of MM into the input well.
Pipette 300 µL of bacterial culture into the output well.
Place the plate back onto the plate stage, wiping the interface first.
Focus on a single channel using the live camera feed after placing the plate stage onto the microscope stage.
Resume flow at 1.00-2.00 dyne/cm2 for approximately 2-4 s to allow cells to enter the experimental channel but not in the serpentine channels.
Leave the plate on the temperature-controlled stage for 1 h to allow for cell attachment.
Open "Multiple Dimensional Acquisition" in the software.
Select "Timelapse", "Multiple Stage Positions", and "Multiple Wavelengths".
Create a Base Name for Saving settings.
Check Increment base name if file exists option.
Click Select Directory to choose the folder for saving files.
Include essential experiment details in Description.
Set Duration of the experimental time to 24 h under the Timelapse tab.
Set Time Interval so images are acquired every 5 min throughout the experiment.
Adjust Number of Time Points based on set parameters.
Use live camera feed in bright field microscope to set stage positions.
Focus on the center of the channel using the 10X objective.
Switch to the 20X objective to find optimal viewing area and focal plane within the channel.
Add position to the list or replace preset channel position with new settings.
Set the number of wavelengths to 3 in the Wavelengths menu.
Select FITC 100% CAM for wavelength 1 (W1) with a 10 ms exposure time.
Select Brightfield 50% CAM 50% VIS for wavelength 2 (W2) with a minimal exposure time of 3 ms.
Set All Closed filter for wavelength 3 (W3).
Stop the manual run in the Control Module.
Set up a new protocol under the Edit Autorun menu with a duration of 24 hours, flowing forward at the desired shear rate.
Add and save the protocol.
Create a new sequence by selecting LB@37degrees as the default fluid for all channels.
Select the protocol with the desired shear rate for channels 1-12 and enable all channels.
Select the protocol with the second desired shear rate for channels 13-24 and enable all channels.
Apply and save the sequence.
Select the saved sequence in the Autorun menu to be used for the autorun.
Pipette a maximum of 1,300 μL of sterile MM into the input well of the microfluidic plate.
Place the plate back onto the plate stage.
Wipe the interface with ethanol and allow it to dry completely.
Seal the plate.
Place the plate stage onto the microscope stage.
Ensure protocols and sequences are set up correctly.
Select Start to begin the autorun.
Click Acquire to start image collection with the microscope.
Adjust focus and placement of all stage positions between image acquisitions.
Select Pause and use live image mode in bright field wavelength.
View each stage position using Go To.
Set new settings by selecting Set to Current.
Click Resume before the next scheduled acquisition time.
Open Review Multidimensional Data under Analysis Tools.
Navigate to the folder with image sequences for the experiment of interest.
Select the base name of the data set of interest from the list of Data Sets in the folder.
Click View to review selected data.
Select a wavelength to review specific data under Wavelength window.
Review the image sequence for each channel by selecting the channel number under Stage Position.
Use video controls to analyze the data for 289 time points, assuming images are obtained every 5 minutes over a 24-hour timeframe.
Take note of usable growth data while monitoring for air bubbles and clogs that may affect biofilm growth within the channel.
Create stacks of images for each channel by selecting Open Special | Build Stack | Numbered Names from the File menu.
Select the first image for the stack in the file folder using the Select First Image button.
Select the last image in the stack using the Select Last Image button and click OK to open the stack in chronological order.
Save stacks under the File menu, Save As as tiff files.
Delete thumb images to save space on the hard drive after creating the image stacks.
Select Save As from the File drop-down menu to save the sequence as a tiff stack.
Under Analysis Tools, click on Calibrate Distances.
Click on the Threshold button while the stack is on the first image of the sequence.
Use Auto Threshold for Light Objects to threshold for fluorescent signal (FITC wavelength).
Use Auto Threshold for Dark Objects to threshold in bright field.
Utilize a channel with non-fluorescent cells to establish any background signal and set the minimum threshold value to exclude signal detected in channels containing these non-fluorescent cells.
Adjust the maximum threshold value via the sliding toolbar or using the Threshold Image under Analysis Tools so that all cells are covered but any background is excluded.
Install a distribution of Python 3.6 that includes standard scientific modules.
Obtain the Biofilm Morphology Suite from GitHub by downloading the zip file.
Unzip the downloaded file and move the code folders to a working directory.
Copy the image stack into the "Coverage" folder.
Navigate to the "Coverage" folder in a terminal window.
Execute the script with the command python bfCoverage.py tiffStackName.tif.
Measure percent thresholded coverage using the generated text file tiffStackName.txt.
Generate a graphics file with the name tiffStackName.png for coverage as a function of time.
Use the same procedure to measure other morphological characteristics: biofilm accumulation, roughness coefficient, and textural entropy.
Execute python bfAcc.py script for the accumulation measurement.
Execute python roughCoef.py script for the roughness coefficient measurement.
Execute python TEvsTime.py script for the textural entropy measurement.
Create overlay stacks including multiple wavelengths if used.
Open all relevant wavelength stacks and calibrate distance.
Select Overlay Images under Analysis Tools.
Set sources as the stacks of interest.
Click on the rainbow circle in the FITC stack and select green color filter.
Adjust overlay to highlight the FITC stack.
Select All Planes for both stacks and click Apply.
Save overlays as described in step 7.5 or as a movie in step 9.2.
To save stacks or overlays as a timelapse movie, click on Make Movie under MM Standard and Stack.
Select the desired source stack or overlay.
Click Save and set file format to Microsoft Video 1 with quality between 70-80.
